explanation: Function notation f(x) is a machine: you feed in an input x and it returns one output f(x). The green dashed line drops from the input on the x-axis up to the curve; the violet dashed line carries that height back to the y-axis as the output. The a, b, c sliders reshape the rule itself, and the readout writes out the full substitution f(x) = a(x)^2 + b(x) + c so you see exactly what 'plug in x' means.
bullets: f(x) names the OUTPUT you get after substituting the input x into the rule.
Each input x gives exactly one output f(x) (that's what makes it a function).
Changing a, b, or c changes the rule, so the same input gives a different output.
